_why: Mutant ids declared BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING for ReadAvrSWAP, each with the reason. `vit_mutate.py --equivalences` reads the KEYS of this object (json.loads then set(...)), so the reasons live in the same file as the claim. A declared equivalence leaves the denominator, so each one is a claim that has to be answerable. ONE is declared here, and it is UNOBSERVABLE rather than equivalent-by-the-standard: the mutated quantity is real, and no input in the admissible domain can carry it to an output. That distinction is stated rather than smoothed over. The other THIRTEEN survivors of the first scoring run (mutation/ReadAvrSWAP.survivors_before_predicate_knobs.json, score 0.8739) are NOT here: they were reachable and the corpus could not reach them, and closing that gap in harness/generate.py killed all thirteen. A survivor is a question about the instrument until the instrument has been asked.
e82a5f90: compare_op '<=' -> '<' at `if (ALREADY_LOADED_LEN <= (int)ErrVar->n_ErrMsg_cap)`, readavrswap.cpp:106. The two forms differ on exactly one input, ALREADY_LOADED_LEN == n_ErrMsg_cap, and ALREADY_LOADED_LEN is the compile-time constant 58 -- the length of 'ERROR: This ROSCO dynamic library has already been loaded.'. n_ErrMsg_cap CANNOT BE 58 on either side of the boundary: the differential harness sets it to `ErrVar_ErrMsg_a.size()`, which is `LEN(ErrMsg) + harness.emit.ALLOC_HEADROOM = n + 4096`, and the integrated build sets it in vit_errorvariables_view.f90:63 to `LEN(src%ErrMsg) + VIT_DEFERRED_CHAR_HEADROOM`, the same 4096. So the capacity is at least 4096 in every configuration this campaign can build, the guard is true in every one of them, and no case at any magnitude, length or flag value can separate `<=` from `<`. SAME SITE, SAME REASON, SAME DECLARATION as ExtController's 11d2c9cc (mutation/ExtController.equivalences.json) -- the two units share the CHARACTER(:), ALLOCATABLE assignment idiom, and this is the second unit to reach it. NOT REMOVED: the guard is what makes an over-long assignment a REFUSAL rather than a truncation, and a truncated error message is the one wrong answer a bit comparison cannot catch. Deleting it to raise the score would delete the property. Note the asymmetry with the OTHER mutant on the same line -- `negate_cond`, which inverts the whole guard -- which the new corpus KILLS: inverting it makes the reference's write not happen at all, and that is observable the moment a case reaches the branch, which is exactly what the predicate-knob block bought.
